transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Damp laundry is most often an airflow problem, so we will start with a free check of the fluff filter in the door opening; heat-pump models like yours often have a second filter at the bottom too. The app shows a picture to help you locate these. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), is the mesh torn, or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the lint filter is" — The fluff/lint filter sits in the door opening or just inside the rim. Lift it out and clear the fluff after every load. Typical layout — your dryer may differ.]

Thank you. The door filter had a thick layer of fluff on it, I'll admit I sometimes forget to clean it. I've cleared it now. I should also say the top of the dryer gets very hot and I often run it while I'm out at work, so I wasn't sure if that's a worry.
Thanks for letting us know about that. Please run a normal drying programme with a normal load of laundry. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?

I haven't run a new load yet, but I'll do that now. Should I also be checking anything else in the meantime, like the condenser at the bottom front? I only ask because the loads have been taking about 2.5 to 3 hours rather than the usual 90 minutes.

Thanks for letting me know about the longer drying times and that you haven’t retested yet. The type of tumble dryer changes what to check next. Is it a vented dryer (a hose out of the back), a condenser dryer with a water container, or a heat-pump dryer?
It's a condenser dryer with a water container, not a vented one and not a heat pump. The water container is the kind you pull out and empty. The model is a Hotpoint TCM580GUK.

Thanks for confirming your Hotpoint TCM580GUK is a condenser dryer. Overloading the drum, or putting in clothes that weren't spun properly in the washer, can make drying take much longer. Ideally, the drum should be no more than about two-thirds full to ensure efficient drying. Was it overloaded or were the clothes very wet going in (and have you changed that), or was it a normal, well-spun load?
It's a normal-sized load, not overloaded, and the clothes come out of a washer that spins at 1400, so they shouldn't be very wet going in.

Thanks for confirming that. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. You can see where this is in the picture shown above. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
Yes, the condenser had lint packed on the fins. I've rinsed it and it looks much cleaner now. The water container was about half full and emptied fine.
Thanks for letting us know about that. Please run a normal drying programme with a normal load. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?
I haven't been able to run the new load yet, I'm about to start it now. Is there anything else I should check while it runs, given how hot the top of the dryer gets?

Thanks for letting us know about the drying issues. Please switch the dryer off, unplug it and let it cool down first. Sensor dryers stop when two metal strips inside the drum near the filter detect that laundry is dry. Fabric conditioner can coat these strips, causing the cycle to end too early. Wipe them with a damp cloth and a little vinegar. Were they coated or dirty (and are they clean now), or were they already clean?

I'm afraid I'm not sure where those metal strips are, as I haven't noticed any inside my drum, so I can't say whether they're dirty. I'm still a bit concerned about how hot the top of the dryer gets, though. Is that something I should be worried about?

When the tumble dryer stops, the pattern of that stop helps us understand what is happening. Please note that if the electrics trip or you smell burning, stop it immediately, leave it switched off, and tell me. If you leave it to cool down for a while, will it start again and carry on, or not at all?
